title: Who's Who: Yvette Saint-Clair
summary: Naturalist of retrievals whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Yvette Saint-Clair (born 1846) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a naturalist of retrievals whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Saint-Clair studies pale mineral deposits and other material brought back by probes, testing whether apparently identical samples share a Referent. Her work suggests that classification itself can affect later custody trials, a claim she treats cautiously.
She has petitioned for specimens to remain unnamed until independent laboratories examine them.

For Alderwick readers, Yvette Saint-Clair stands not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
